952.headline: How this game pays out

959.body:
Most of the tickets for "LOTERIA®" are sold. The top prize count has held, with two of eight still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "LOTERIA®" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
959.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

972.body:
$8 Million Money Maker's prizes make it a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

Everything above about "$8 Million Money Maker" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
972.headline: The prize mix in this game

975.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "$1,000,000 Money Rush", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is well into its run, with two of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

If "$1,000,000 Money Rush" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
975.headline: How much has sold

976.body:
All the top prizes on "100X The Cash" have been claimed. That lowers the biggest prize from $2 million to $10,000. That level still has two unclaimed. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

If you play "100X The Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
976.headline: The advertised top prize is gone

980.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "20X The Cash", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is past the halfway point of its run, with three of eight top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

If "20X The Cash" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
980.headline: How far along this game is

981.body:
"50X The Cash" has one of six top prizes left and is in the last part of its run. Most of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

The table below shows the full count for "50X The Cash", with every prize level included.
981.headline: Early stage or late

985.body:
About half of the tickets for "MAX-A-MILLION" have been sold. The game is in the middle of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Twelve of MAX-A-MILLION's 25 top prizes can still be won.

Tomorrow's count on "MAX-A-MILLION" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
985.headline: How far along this game is

988.body:
"Emerald 10's" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of its unclaimed prize money, most is in wins under $2,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

Every line of Emerald 10's's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
988.headline: How the prize money is divided

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" is in the second half of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Everything above about "LADY LUCK" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
990.headline: Tickets sold so far

992.body:
The most common win left on "$2 MILLION VAULT" is $20. The second biggest prize left is $100,000, and one of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The numbers for "$2 MILLION VAULT" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
992.headline: A close look at the prizes

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has gone five months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About three-quarters of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $5,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything here about "$5,000 Triple Play" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through November 9.
993.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

994.body:
The most common win left on "$25,000 Triple Play" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $3,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Today's free summary of "$25,000 Triple Play" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
994.headline: What's actually left to win

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has had no $200,000 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Every line of $200,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
995.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

996.body:
The top prize count on "$1,000,000 Triple Play" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has four of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
996.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed
